ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In order to study the effect of temperature on the activity of a certain enzyme, three experimental groups were set up: group A (20℃), group B (40℃), and group C (60℃), and the product concentration of each group at different reaction times was measured (other conditions were the same). The results are shown in the figure. Answer the question: under the three temperature conditions, which group has the highest enzyme activity?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the horizontal axis is reaction time, and the vertical axis is product concentration; the legend shows three curves of 20℃, 40℃, and 60℃. The solid line corresponding to 40℃ rises the fastest within the same reaction time, has the greatest slope, and reaches a relatively high product concentration earlier; the curve corresponding to 20℃ rises more slowly; the dashed line corresponding to 60℃ quickly tends toward a lower plateau. Then reason: enzyme activity can usually be expressed by the amount of product generated per unit time, that is, the greater the slope of the curve of product concentration changing with time, the higher the enzyme activity. In the question stem, group A is 20℃, group B is 40℃, and group C is 60℃, so the one with the highest enzyme activity is group B corresponding to 40℃.
